scope: Theorem 17.3 (Bilateral subsequential limit at all time scales) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 208-209. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For a positive integer N set j(N) = ⌊log2 N⌋, BN = Aj(N). Then BN → ∞. From every sequence Nr → ∞ one can extract a subsequence such that the bilateral contours and all their local certificate data, in time units Nr and cost units BNr , converge jointly. The continuum background is the fixed-unit √ 2-quantum cone decorated by its area-parametrized SLE8. For one deterministic λ ∈ [C−, 2p C+], (17.17) 208 its limiting local passage rule is FU (x, y) = λDh(x, y; U) (17.18) for every open U and every x, y joined by a path compactly in U. The equality uses the internal length metric on U, equivalently exhaustion by compactly confined paths, and includes the upper realization and lower subpath-extraction assertions with open margins. There is also the following uniform discrete estimate. For each fixed T < ∞ there is KT < ∞ such that, for every integer N ≥ 1 and every translated integer interval I of length |I| ≤ TN, diam(V (GI), dI) BN k ≤ KT  |I| + 1 N s . (17.19) The corresponding curve-time modulus on each bounded window is uniform, with any exponent smaller than s − 1/k. The fixed-interval endpoint kth moments are uniformly integrable along these extractions.
